correctness.rationale: The complete chain groups are explicitly calculated: 2m vertices, 3m-2 arrows and m-1 independent square-difference two-chains; every invariant chain in degrees >=3 vanishes by unique forbidden-deletion faces. The three relevant ranks are 2m-1, m-1, and m-1 for the two-step composition when N>=3 (zero for N=2). The rank formula for Mayer homology then gives each displayed case, including empty ranges. A standalone exact finite-field verifier independently reconstructs allowed paths and nonallowed face constraints for 35 (N,m) cases, all indices q, and checks the true rank matrices. The general proof is independent of those finite tests.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification for the smallest nontrivial directed rectangular strip, extending published one-square, cubic-root motif computations. The whole family remains ordinarily path-acyclic, yet the Mayer theory develops m-1 independent degree-two classes precisely for N>=4 and q>=3; the jump isolates a higher-order phenomenon that a finite table or classical graph homology cannot see. The proof also gives an all-length cutoff on invariant path chains and a reusable cancellation mechanism for sparse commutative squares.
